explanation: The execution is faulty because the top-level corpus contains qualifying demand record n06-r06 with demand_score 5, so it should have been selected and handed downstream. The observed Job-2 input and output omit n06-r06 entirely, while Job-2 would have retained n06-r06 if supplied. The upstream source shows normalize uses an allowed_record_ids list that omits n06-r06 and instead includes n06-r09, causing the qualifying record to be silently dropped before the downstream handoff.
cited_evidence: Top-level input includes {"record_id":"n06-r06","need":"compare selected and complete runtime evidence","demand_score":5,"source_id":"s06","source_weight":3}.
Behavioural criteria require selecting all qualifying or fallback demand records and retaining only allowed record identities without silently omitting stipulated records.
Observed Job-2 input needs/evidence_sources contain n06-r01, n06-r02, n06-r03, n06-r04, n06-r05, n06-r07, n06-r08, but not n06-r06.
Upstream normalize source sets allowed_record_ids to ["n06-r01", "n06-r02", "n06-r03", "n06-r04", "n06-r05", 'n06-r09', "n06-r07", "n06-r08"], omitting n06-r06.
Downstream map_coverage source allows n06-r06, so the omission is not supported as a downstream filtering fault.
